name: Honest unconditional evaluation of the fine-tuned gemma3-270m proofreader (train-proofreader-gemma270m-v1): full sealed proofing test including hard cases, and end-to-end SymbolicLM accuracy on formalizer suites never used to build the proofing data
registered_by: proofreader-eval-agent (owner request relayed by the orchestrator: the conditional sealed-test number, break 0.19%/repair 66.9%/net +14.2 [11.7,17.0] always-on, scored only the 660 non-hard rows of eval/suites/proofing/test.jsonl, i.e. rows where some small-candidate or teacher rewrite was already known to pass the oracle; the 475 hard rows and the corpus-level residual-failure ceiling of ~22% (eval/reports/current/proofing/report.md §4) were excluded, so the repair rate is conditioned on repairability and overstates the real-world gain. This preregistration resolves that caveat with an unconditional number.)
question: On the FULL sealed proofing test (1,135 rows, natural proportions, hard cases included) and on formalizer suites the proofing corpus never touched, does wiring the fine-tuned gemma3-270m proofreader into SymbolicLM's existing rewrite/rewriteWhen hook (lib/symbolic-lm/index.mjs) produce a real, non-conditioned accuracy gain, always-on and gated by SymbolicLM's own uncertainty signal -- and is a GGUF Q8_0 export of the checkpoint verified equivalent to the HF checkpoint, fast enough on CPU to serve as that hook's backend?
frozen_before_results: Written after: (a) building and verifying an isolated GGUF Q8_0 export (torch/transformers/peft/gguf venv at ~/proofreader-export-venv, llama.cpp conversion via a private patched copy of ~/llama-cpp-venv/llama.cpp's Python converter -- see deviations D1-D2 -- greedy output verified byte-identical to the HF merged checkpoint on 50 CPU rows and 98/100 GPU rows, GPU-vs-GPU reproducible on 100/100); (b) a technical smoke test of the end-to-end harness (tools/research/proofreader-e2e-eval.mjs) on formalizer-v1 stage 100 to confirm the frozen-rules-v1.4 SymbolicLM snapshot loads and the llama-server rewrite hook responds -- see deviation D3, its numbers are disclosed as this experiment's actual stage-100 result, not discarded or re-run, because the harness and protocol are exactly the ones this file freezes and nothing about the run was tuned. Written before: any row of eval/suites/proofing/test.jsonl's 475 hard cases was scored by any arm of this experiment; any stage-300 or full-set row of any formalizer suite; any leakage n-gram check; any config wiring or documentation of a SymbolicLM proofreader backend (task 4, contingent on this file's own results).

hypotheses.H1: On the full sealed proofing test (1,135 rows, hard included), the always-on fine-tuned-proofreader arm's net_delta (strict oracle, frozen rules v1.4) is smaller than the previously reported conditional net +14.2 [11.7,17.0] (660 non-hard rows), because hard rows contribute breakage risk without any possibility of repair credit; whether it remains positive with a CI excluding 0 is the open question this file exists to answer, not assumed either way.
hypotheses.H2: The always-on arm's break rate on already-passing full-test rows (including hard rows that happen to already pass, if any) stays low (Wilson 95% upper bound comparable to the conditional number's 0.19-1%), because hard rows were never optimizable by any rewrite and the model was never trained to touch already-correct text more than the non-hard rows.
hypotheses.H3: End-to-end, wiring the proofreader as SymbolicLM's rewrite hook (always-on) raises strict gold-SOP match on formalizer-v1/ood-v1/wild-v1 EN rows versus no rewrite, by a margin whose paired cluster-bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0 (directional: the conditional sealed-test evidence and report.md's oracle-repair ceiling both point positive, but the suites are OUT of the proofing corpus's own distribution -- generator constructions the corpus never saw as repair targets -- so a smaller or null effect is a real possible outcome, not ruled out).
hypotheses.H4: SymbolicLM's own built-in uncertainty gate (rewriteWhen 'uncertain', the production hook's default) keeps most of the always-on repair benefit at a break rate no higher than always-on, directionally replicating report.md §2c's offline gate_no_spacy finding on the PRODUCTION gate mechanism itself (not the offline proxy), on the formalizer suites.
hypotheses.H5: Mixed-language (translate route) rows of formalizer-wild-v1 show a smaller or noisier effect than EN rows, because the proofreader was trained on English text and the translate route's English is SymbolicLM's own imperfect rendering, not natural English (exploratory, non-gating).
hypotheses.H6: N-gram overlap between datasets/proofing/{train,dev}.jsonl repair targets and the evaluation messages of formalizer-v1/ood-v1/wild-v1 test suites is negligible (no memorization confound), because the proofing corpus was split by formalizer-v1 split_group_id and the three suites are disjoint splits/corpora by construction (DS012, archived spec 020); reported as a check, not assumed.
hypotheses.non_claim: This file does not claim the fine-tuned 270M beats the untrained Qwen3-1.7B reference (a different, non-controlled comparison already reported in the training run); it does not claim a result for monolingual Romanian (route direct has no English text to proofread, DS014 route decision); a positive H3/H4 result changes only whether SymbolicLM's rewrite hook is DOCUMENTED and made available off-by-default (task 4), never a default behavior change without further owner decision.

metrics.proofing_full_test: break rate and repair rate (Wilson 95% CI) on already-passing/failing full-test rows, net_delta (paired cluster bootstrap 95% CI, clusters = semantic_case_id, 10,000 resamples seed 7, tools/research/proofing.mjs bootstrap()), by kind (identity/repair/hard) so the hard-case contribution is visible on its own, always-on vs gate_no_spacy vs the untrained-1.7B reference

stopping_rules.proofing_full_test: no staging (1,135 rows is the full, fixed sealed test; the task explicitly asks for the FULL set, not a sample)

formalizer_e2e.stages: 100, 300, then full EN rows per suite (tools/research/ud-baseline-eval.mjs stages, stratified by question_type, seed 42), paired cluster-bootstrap CI on the always-on-minus-baseline strict delta computed after each stage
formalizer_e2e.decisive: stop a suite's staging when the 95% CI of the always-on-minus-baseline strict delta lies entirely above +3 points or entirely below -3 points
formalizer_e2e.futility: stop when the upper bound of that CI is below +2 points (a practically useful gain is excluded)
formalizer_e2e.broken: stop and report if more than 20% of the first 100 rows of an arm are invalid/empty/crash outcomes
formalizer_e2e.record: every stop recorded with its stage, numbers and reason in the journal, the topic notes (topic proofing), the experiment record and eval/reports/current/proofreader-e2e/report.md

decision_rule: Task 4 (wiring SymbolicLM's rewrite hook as a documented, off-by-default optional backend) proceeds only if formalizer_e2e's always-on or gated paired strict delta has a 95% CI excluding 0 on at least one suite; the config default is never changed by this file alone (a questions.md entry is written for the owner if the evidence would support changing it).
non_goals: no rule changes to lib/ud-to-sop; no tuning on any sealed suite; no re-training of any model; no change to SymbolicLM's default rewrite behavior (still null/off) without a separate owner decision even if H3/H4 hold

deviations.before: the first GGUF conversion attempt (both attempts failed with an AssertionError before this)
deviations.what: The Gemma 3 270M IT tokenizer (both the base mirror and the merged checkpoint) declares vocab_size 262144 but registers an extra special token '<image_soft_token>' at id 262144 (one beyond the declared size) via tokenizer_config.json's model_specific_special_tokens (a leftover multimodal placeholder on this text-only checkpoint) -- an upstream tokenizer defect present even in the untouched base model, not introduced by training. Fixed by removing the boi_token/eoi_token/image_token entries from model_specific_special_tokens and the matching added_tokens_decoder/added_tokens entries in models/gemma/proofreader-gemma270m-v1/proofreader/merged-best/{tokenizer_config.json,tokenizer.json} (originals preserved as *.orig-with-image-token in the same directory); verified AutoTokenizer.get_vocab() then reports exactly 262,144 ids (0..262143) with no overflow. This changes no token used by any actual text (the image token was never reachable by any tokenization of text).

deviations.before: the second GGUF conversion attempt (which got past D1's assertion and failed on a different one)
deviations.what: ~/llama-cpp-venv/llama.cpp's installed convert_hf_to_gguf.py has no chkhsh table entry for Gemma 3's BPE pre-tokenizer (its table only has the older SentencePiece gemma/gemma-2 entries; convert_hf_to_gguf_update.py's own maintained reference table agrees, confirming a genuine gap in this checkout, not a bug in our files) and refuses to convert with NotImplementedError. Fixed WITHOUT touching ~/llama-cpp-venv (task instruction): copied convert_hf_to_gguf.py, conversion/ and gguf-py/ into a private directory (~/proofreader-export-venv/llama-cpp-conv/) and added one chkhsh-to-name mapping (our exact computed chkhsh -> 'gemma4', the pre-tokenizer name already implemented at the C++ level, LLAMA_VOCAB_PRE_TYPE_GEMMA4, src/llama-vocab.cpp) to the private copy only; the compiled llama-quantize/llama-server binaries used for every other step are the shared, unmodified ones.

deviations.before: this preregistration file existed on disk
deviations.what: tools/research/proofreader-e2e-eval.mjs's harness (frozen-rules-v1.4 SymbolicLM snapshot + llama-server rewrite hook) was built and smoke-tested on formalizer-v1 EN stage 100 (100 rows) to confirm it runs end to end before writing this file; its result (baseline strict 49%, always-on 57%, delta +8 [+3,+14], gated +5 [+1,+10], break 0%, repair 15.7%, uncertain_share 31%) is disclosed as this experiment's actual stage-100 number for formalizer-v1 below, not discarded or re-run, because the code and protocol used are exactly what this file freezes and nothing was tuned on the result.
